info.title: The registry's public API
info.description: Read and write the registry's own layer (repositories and their papers, research issues, stars, follows, notifications, outgoing webhooks, commit statuses) with a personal token. GitHub's own objects stay GitHub's: its API serves them. The reference, with examples: /developers/.

x-scopes.repos:read: read the registry's layer over repositories: their papers, their state, the commit statuses posted to it
x-scopes.research:read: read research issues and their comments
x-scopes.research:write: open, comment on, edit, close and reopen research issues, as you
x-scopes.social:read: read your stars, lists and follows, people's public profiles and your feed
x-scopes.social:write: star, list, follow and watch, and change your profile, as you
x-scopes.notifications:read: read your notifications (the registry's own inbox)
x-scopes.notifications:write: mark your notifications read, done or saved, and unsubscribe
x-scopes.hooks:read: read your outgoing webhooks and their deliveries
x-scopes.hooks:write: make, change, test, redeliver and delete your outgoing webhooks
x-scopes.statuses:write: post commit statuses on the repositories the registry knows (a CI or a reproduction service)
x-scopes.security:write: upload code-scanning results (SARIF) from your CI, for the repositories the registry knows

token.description: A personal token of the registry (oscr_pat_…), made on /settings/tokens/: scoped, expiring, revocable.

ApiVersion.name: X-Api-Version
ApiVersion.description: The version asked, a date (2026-09-29); none: the current one.

get.summary: This index: the version, the routes, how to authenticate.
Whose token this is (public handles), its scopes, its expiry.

304.description: Not modified: the ETag sent in If-None-Match still holds (not counted against the rate limit).

get.summary: The token's use of its rate limits (never counted).

get.summary: What a command line needs to sign in: the GitHub App's public client id (for GitHub's own device flow, asked of GitHub directly), the device flow's routes, the scopes.

post.summary: Start a command line's sign-in: a device code (kept by the command line), a user code of 8 letters, and the approval page's address; it lives 15 minutes and writes nothing.

scopes.description: What the token may do, as scopes (required).

days.description: Its life, 1 to 366 days (30 by default).

name.description: Its name in your settings (40 characters).

post.summary: Poll a sign-in (at most every 5 seconds): 400 authorization_pending, slow_down, access_denied or expired_token; once approved on the page, the token, answered once.
The token that makes this call revokes itself at once (a command line's sign-out). It never revokes another.

(none).description: An empty object: the token in the Authorization header is the one revoked.
